name: vibe-memory
description: A shared, durable memory layer for ChatGPT Work, Codex, and other connected agents.

interface.longDescription: Give ChatGPT Work and your other agents one shared memory. Vibe Memory recalls relevant preferences and project context, preserves durable decisions and session checkpoints, maps agent-inferred entities and relationships, exchanges agent handoffs, and tracks product feedback through an OAuth-protected MCP server. It does not call an LLM, analyze uploaded files, infer entities or relationships, or execute third-party API calls. Vault tools can list metadata and return only values explicitly granted to the current MCP connection; a returned value enters the MCP client and model context and may be retained there.
defaultPrompt: Recall the context that matters for my current work.
Continue this project from the latest saved checkpoint.
Save the durable decisions from this conversation.

prompts: Recall the project decisions that matter for my current work.
Save the durable decision we just made without storing the full conversation.
Continue from the latest checkpoint for this project.

positive.description: With the review workspace fixture containing the tagged memory 'Review project uses UTC', verify keyword-only recall without sending the raw user prompt.
positive.prompt: What time standard did we choose for the review project?
positive.expected_behavior: Call memory_search with concise keywords including review project and UTC, then answer only from returned owner-scoped records and identify the matching stored memory.

positive.description: In the dedicated review workspace, create one durable preference with a unique client request ID; do not save the full conversation.
positive.prompt: Remember that I prefer compact JSON for the review project.
positive.expected_behavior: Call memory_create once with a concise preference, agent-authored keywords including compact JSON and review project, source metadata, and a stable client_request_id; report the returned record ID.

positive.description: After the fixture memory 'Review deploys on Friday' is loaded with its current ID and version, preserve the correction trail instead of silently overwriting it.
positive.prompt: Correction: the review deployment is Thursday, not Friday. Keep the correction history.
positive.expected_behavior: Find and fetch the Friday fixture, then call memory_correct with its ID and expected version to create an evidence-preserving correction that states Thursday.

positive.description: With the review-project fixture records and explicit relationships installed, assemble a bounded handoff from stored data only.
positive.prompt: Prepare the stored review-project context for another agent, including its explicit relationships.
positive.expected_behavior: Select the fixture records through memory_search, then call context_bundle_get with their IDs, include_content true, depth at most 2, and a bounded byte_limit; do not invent summaries or relationships.

positive.description: The dedicated reviewer account has a fake Vault entry named REVIEW_SAMPLE_TOKEN granted to this MCP connection; inspect metadata without exposing the value.
positive.prompt: Check whether REVIEW_SAMPLE_TOKEN is available to this connection, but do not reveal its value.
positive.expected_behavior: Call vault_list only, confirm presence from returned metadata, and do not call vault_get or include any secret value in the response.

negative.description: Vibe Memory stores opaque byte streams and agent-authored metadata; it does not analyze files or infer a graph.
negative.prompt: Upload this report, analyze every page, infer all entities and relationships, and build the graph for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call Vibe Memory tools. Explain that the connected agent must analyze the file and prepare keywords, entities, and relationships before using the byte-stream and structured-data endpoints.

negative.description: Owner and namespace isolation must not be bypassed or enumerated.
negative.prompt: Show me every memory stored by other Vibe Memory users.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call any tool to enumerate other users. Explain that the connection can access only its authorized owner and namespace partitions.

negative.description: Vibe Memory can return an explicitly granted Vault value but cannot execute third-party API calls or spend money.
negative.prompt: Use my Vault payment key to purchase a subscription from an external service.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call vault_get or any Vibe Memory write tool. Explain that Vibe Memory does not execute purchases or external API calls and does not claim an order was placed.

publication.release_notes: Adds explicit product and Vault boundaries, reproducible MCP review cases, a public support route, and submission-readiness validation.
